name: Dorsal hump rasping (DIY)

card.summary: Do-it-yourself filing or striking of a nasal bump to flatten the profile; surgical literature describes dorsal hump reduction as a surgeon-performed procedure.
card.aka: Home hump filing, nose bone smashing
card.note: Surgical references describe dorsal reduction as an operation with anesthesia and sterile technique.

quick.overview:
Dorsal hump rasping refers to attempts to reduce a bump on the bridge of the nose without a surgeon, by filing or hitting it, with the aim of a straighter profile from brow to tip.

In medical references, hump reduction is a step within rhinoplasty carried out by trained surgeons, who cut the cartilage, chisel the bone and smooth it with rasps. No published study evaluates a home version.
quick.how: In surgery, the bony and cartilaginous bump on the nasal dorsum is reduced with instruments under anesthesia, after which the nose is typically splinted and taped for about a week [1]. Home attempts borrow the filing or striking idea; no standard method is documented.
quick.risks: Nasal bones and cartilage support breathing as well as shape. Surgeons describe an open roof gap that can follow shaving a hump unless it is closed with controlled bone cuts, and rhinoplasty references list contour deformities and a revision rate of roughly 5 to 20 percent [1][3]. Injury, infection and airway problems are general concerns for any nasal trauma. No study evaluates the DIY practice.

lead: Dorsal hump rasping (DIY) is the name given to attempts to lower a bump on the nasal bridge at home by filing or striking it, with the goal of a straighter nose profile without surgery. The bridge of the nose is one of the most visible profile features, and a smoother line from brow to tip is what people attempting it are after.

In professional practice, hump reduction is a step of rhinoplasty: the surgeon cuts the cartilage portion with a scalpel, chisels the bony portion with an osteotome, and then smooths the cut bone with rasps of various grades. [1] The home practice borrows the rasping step. Clinic and surgeon writing describes the cause of a hump as mostly inherited, with septal cartilage growing faster than the nasal bones, or as the result of an injury that healed with extra bone. [3]

After surgery the nose is taped and fitted with a protective splint, the dressing is typically removed after about a week, and swelling can take at least a year to settle. [1] Rhinoplasty references list complications such as pollybeak, saddle nose, inverted-V, rocker and open roof deformity, and report that revision is needed in roughly 5 to 20 percent of cases. [1] No published study evaluates self-performed hump reduction.

chain: Bony and cartilage hump on the nasal bridge is reduced
Profile line from brow to tip becomes straighter
angle.text: The aim is a straighter nasal profile by lowering the dorsal hump. In surgical practice this is done by a surgeon with osteotome and rasp; the home version is described only as a practice some people attempt.

paras: Rhinoplasty references describe surgeon-performed reshaping: cartilage is cut with a scalpel, bone is chiselled with an osteotome and the cut bone is sculpted and smoothed with rasps. [1] The nose is then taped and splinted, with the dressing typically removed about a week later, and prolonged swelling is part of recovery. [1]

An Istanbul clinic's explainer says shaving the peak of a hump leaves a flat gap called an open roof, which can produce a wide, boxy bridge if left alone. Surgeons close it with controlled bone cuts called osteotomies, and often place spreader grafts to keep the airway open. It also describes preservation rhinoplasty as an alternative that lowers the bridge from underneath. [3]

Rhinoplasty references say results can be unpredictable, that revision surgery is needed in roughly 5 to 20 percent of cases, and that smoking impairs healing. [1] Named contour problems after surgical hump reduction include open roof, inverted-V and saddle nose deformities. [1] Facial feminization surgery references note that reducing nasal size carries a risk of impairing nasal valve function, which relates to breathing. [2]

A surgeon's article on do-it-yourself nose-reshaping devices, which is a related but different practice, warns of permanent bruising, deformities, scars and infection, and says that in teenagers such devices can interfere with natural development. [4] No study evaluates outcomes or injuries from self-performed filing or striking.
